text:
Nora Singh: Seeing a spike of GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast2b since 07:12 UTC. Nodes report transient NIC resets and then kubelet marking GPUs NotReady. Small inference jobs piling pending.

Diego Ramos: Scheduler logs show many 'node tainted: gpu-net-fault' events and preemption churn. bindLatency up ~40ms.

infra-bot: Alert: gpu_eviction_rate(ap-southeast2b) > 2.5x baseline. Ticket INC-2334 opened.

Nora Singh: Quick triage: cordoned 2 flapping nodes (ap2b-node-21/34) and drained them. Launched +3 warm gpu nodes to absorb backlog.

Diego Ramos: Short-term mitigation: apply soft taint `gpu-net-suspect=true:PreferNoSchedule` on nodes in rack-7; reduce preemption aggressiveness for this AZ to prevent oscillation.

Nora Singh: Logs snippet from node:
```
May 18 07:11:58 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:af:00.1: link reset
May 18 07:12:01 kubelet: device plugin: GPU gone
```
Conntrack counters also look high on some hosts.

Opsana: Action items: 1) run conntrack audit and bump if needed; 2) schedule NIC firmware check for rack-7; 3) add scheduler weight for `net-stable=true` for GPU-bound pods; 4) cost owner: pre-authorize up to +$900/day if autoscaler remains bumped.

Diego Ramos: After cordons+scale, eviction rate down ~30% in 12m. I'll follow up with a canary to tweak preemption backoff tonight.

Nora Singh: Will update INC-2334 with timeline and next steps. Thanks.
